title: An email about my city
prompt: Reply to someone asking about your city. Use separate paragraphs for where you grew up, life in the city and things a visitor can do.
checks: I used a suitable opening and closing.
I organized ideas into paragraphs.
I answered the questions clearly.
I checked question word order and punctuation.

title: An advertisement for a possession
prompt: Write an ad for an item you want to sell. Describe its condition, age, color, features and price. Use one and ones to avoid repetition.
checks: I gave useful product information.
I described its condition honestly.
I used one/ones clearly.
I stated a price and checked the wording.

title: A volunteer application
prompt: Apply to help at a city race. Explain your motivation, previous experience and useful qualities. Include directions between two places.
checks: I answered all parts of the application.
I explained why I would be a good volunteer.
I used city and direction vocabulary.
I checked articles, grammar and punctuation.

title: A surprise-party invitation
prompt: Write an invitation to a surprise birthday party. Explain the place, times and preparations. Connect events with to start, at the same time and after that.
checks: I included the main event details.
I distinguished plans from sudden decisions.
I used expressions that order events.
I made the surprise and preparation clear.

title: A story with a surprise
prompt: Write a short true or invented story about a childhood fear or a surprising experience. Use simple language, a shared experience, details that show feelings and a surprise.
checks: I used simple past and past continuous correctly.
I showed feelings with details.
I included something readers can relate to.
I gave the story a surprising ending.

title: A point of view about flying ambulances
prompt: Write a comment about flying ambulances. Say whether you think they are useful, give reasons and use a question to make one of your points.
checks: I stated a clear opinion.
I supported it with reasons.
I used a real conditional correctly.
I used a question to make a point.

title: A movie recommendation
prompt: Write a conversation recommending a movie. Name its genre, give a short description and explain at least three reasons why you like it.
checks: I organized the description and reasons clearly.
I used movie vocabulary.
I gave at least three reasons.
I checked comparisons and past habits where relevant.

title: A response to time-saving advice
prompt: Respond to Andrew's tips: keep things in a regular place, and remember you can refuse an invitation when you need personal time. Say whether the tips would help you and give examples.
checks: I gave my own view of the tips.
I included examples or reasons.
I used time expressions clearly.
I distinguished ongoing activities from completed results.

title: A résumé
prompt: Write the main parts of a résumé for an invented person with an interesting job. Include experience, skills and education. Use parallel structures in lists.
checks: I organized experience, skills and education.
I used parallel wording in bullet points.
I included relevant employment vocabulary.
I checked spelling and dates.

title: Product feedback
prompt: Write feedback about an everyday product such as shampoo or dish soap. Explain why you buy it, what you like and what you dislike. Contrast ideas with however and although.
checks: I gave specific positive and negative feedback.
I used however and although accurately.
I used product and material vocabulary.
I checked passive verb forms where I used them.

title: A story about helping
prompt: Tell a story about helping someone or receiving help. Explain what happened and how you felt. Contrast viewpoints with on the one hand and on the other hand where useful.
checks: I told events in a clear order.
I explained feelings and the result.
I contrasted viewpoints clearly.
I checked phrasal verbs and object position.

title: An anecdote about a lesson
prompt: Describe a mistake you made in the past and the lesson you learned. Explain what happened, how people felt and what you would do differently now. Vary your expressions to avoid repetition.
checks: I told a clear anecdote.
I explained the lesson.
I used reported speech or indefinite pronouns accurately.
I varied wording and avoided unnecessary repetition.
